name: Push to Talk
plain: Walkie talkie voice channels that start in the background from a push.
meaning: Gives apps a system managed channel to open the microphone from a push, with a clear UI.

android.permission: FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE (normal), RECORD_AUDIO; foreground service type microphone
android.note: No platform PTT framework; Android 17 hardens background audio

ios.prompt_ui: System PTT UI and microphone prompt
ios.note: Apple's system UI shows channel, orange dot while active

limits.headline: Can start walkie talkie voice from the background on iPhone, with microphone consent
limits.user_action: You open a channel and hold to talk, or someone starts talking to you
can: Wake the app by push to start a live voice channel on iPhone
Show a system screen that names the channel
Use the microphone while you talk, with an orange dot showing
cannot: Use the microphone without your allowing it
Do this on iPhone without Apple's approval for the app
Use a built in walkie talkie system on Android, which has none
Hide that the microphone is on, since the orange dot is always shown
limits.reach_label: While you talk in a channel
limits.differs: iPhone has an Apple walkie talkie framework (iOS 16). Android has none, so apps use a normal microphone prompt and notification.

story.what_it_is: A walkie talkie style feature where a push starts a voice channel in the background.

marketing.name: Push to Talk framework
marketing.pitch: Apple provides a system framework and screen for walkie talkie style apps that talk over a push.

story.for_you: You press talk and your voice goes out instantly to a group. You see a system screen and an orange dot while the microphone is on.
story.for_makers: Makers of dispatch and team apps get a trusted way to start live voice from a push. Apple adds a clear screen so it cannot be used to listen in secret.

use_cases.example: A warehouse team talks across the floor with one tap.
A squad in a team game talks over a push channel in the background.
A family app lets kids and parents send quick voice notes in real time.
A ski patrol or event crew talks over a live group channel.
A fleet dispatcher speaks to every truck with one press.
A walkie talkie style social app lets friends drop in on each other.
A guard team uses push to talk to share alerts quickly.

story.android_note: Android has no platform push to talk. Apps use microphone prompts and a notification.
story.ios_note: iOS needs Apple approval, a system screen and an orange dot while active.

technical_bounds: Android has no dedicated PTT API
